summary: The paper proposes SteerVAD, a framework that identifies discriminative attention heads (LAEs) inside a frozen MLLM via a gradient-free separability score and then applies a small learned context-dependent anisotropic scaling to those heads for video anomaly detection. The geometric framing is interesting, and the ablations, stability analysis, and data-efficiency study are appreciated, but the reported SOTA gains over prior tuning-free methods are marginal (+0.43% AUC / +0.87% AP), the comparison table lacks error bars, and the 'tuning-free' positioning is misleading because the HMC and scorer are trained with labels on 1% data while baselines like LAVAD/EventVAD require no supervised training. Novelty is incremental relative to established activation-steering / representation-engineering work in LLM interpretability, which is not cited or contrasted, and generality is under-supported (single backbone, two datasets).
strengths: Clear geometric reframing of MLLM-based VAD as manifold rectification, with a coherent two-stage design (RSA to pick heads, HMC to modulate them).
Well-designed ablations covering both HMC components (GSG vs LGM vs static/additive steering) and expert-selection heuristics (random, positional, RSA).
Stability analysis across 10 seeds and a data-efficiency sweep from 1% to 100% strengthen the claim that the identified LAEs reflect intrinsic model structure rather than data artifacts.
Method is lightweight (small MLP + low-rank adapters + logistic scorer), and the anisotropic scaling formulation h' = h(1 + s_global · g_i) is simple and clearly stated.

key_concerns.issue: Category positioning is misleading. The paper claims 'tuning-free' SOTA but trains the HMC (MLP + K adapters) and a logistic scorer with labeled BCE on 1% data, while the tuning-free baselines it beats (LAVAD, EventVAD, VERA, zero-shot CLIP/ImageBind) use no supervised training. This is few-shot supervised, not tuning-free.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Re-label the method as 'few-shot / parameter-efficient' or introduce a separate row in Table 1 for methods that train a small head on labeled calibration data; compare directly against weakly-supervised methods at 1% supervision to contextualize gains.

key_concerns.issue: The reported gains over the closest tuning-free baseline (HiProbeVAD) are +0.43% AUC on UCF-Crime and +0.87% AP on XD-Violence, and Table 1 reports single-run numbers with no error bars or significance tests. The seed study in Table 3 gives σ≈0.04% for the model but says nothing about baseline variance, so it is unclear the improvement is statistically real.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Report mean ± std over multiple seeds for both SteerVAD and re-run baselines under matched backbone/frame budgets, and add a paired significance test.

key_concerns.issue: Related-work positioning omits the very literature this method belongs to: activation steering / representation engineering / Inference-Time Intervention (ITI), attention-head ablation and function-vector work in mechanistic interpretability. The claim that 'the application of dynamic, context-dependent rectification of internal geometric structures … remains an unexplored frontier' overstates novelty without contrasting these lines of work.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add a dedicated subsection contrasting SteerVAD against activation-steering / ITI / task-vector / representation-engineering methods, and clarify what is genuinely new (task, dynamic gating, anisotropy) versus adopted.

key_concerns.issue: Generality is under-supported for the paper's framing. Only one MLLM backbone (InternVL3) and two VAD benchmarks are used; the argument that LAEs are 'intrinsic functional circuits' would be much stronger if the method (or at least RSA) transferred across MLLMs (e.g., Qwen-VL, LLaVA, VideoLLaMA).
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add at least one additional MLLM backbone and one out-of-distribution VAD benchmark (e.g., ShanghaiTech or MSAD), and report whether the identified LAE layer indices co-vary or transfer.

key_concerns.issue: The 100% identical LAE-selection across 10 seeds (Table 3) is suspicious unless it is clarified what was actually varied. RSA is deterministic given a fixed 1% subset, so if only training seeds (not the calibration subsample) changed, the result is trivial rather than a robustness signal.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Explicitly re-sample the 1% calibration subset per seed and re-run RSA; report the Jaccard overlap of the selected head set across those resamples.

key_concerns.issue: Reproducibility gaps: the anomaly scorer's aggregation, HMC hidden/bottleneck dimensions, exact frozen-token used for context vector c, and the RSA feature (which token position within a head is used?) are underspecified in the main text and deferred to appendices B/A.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Move the key architectural sizes (d_hidden, r, dhead per LAE), the feature-extraction protocol per head, and the HMC training hyperparameters into the main-body Methods.

key_concerns.issue: The manifold-hypothesis framing (§3.1 and citations to Whiteley et al., Genovese et al., Boissonnat & Ghosh) is decorative — nothing in the actual method uses topology or manifold geometry beyond a Fisher-like inter/intra scatter ratio and an elementwise (1 + s·g) rescale. This risks overclaiming a 'geometric' contribution.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Either tone down the manifold framing and describe the method as a Fisher-ratio head selector plus learned gating, or add a concrete geometric quantity (e.g., pre/post-rectification linear separability, curvature, or manifold-distance metric) tied to the rectification.

key_concerns.issue: Table 1's parameter column obscures fairness: SteerVAD is listed at ~8B (the frozen backbone), same as VERA/HiProbeVAD, but the additional HMC parameters trained on labels are not tabulated; conversely, tuning-free ZS-CLIP/ImageBind sit at very different backbone scales.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add a 'trainable parameters' column and a 'labeled supervision used' column so readers can see backbone size, extra trained parameters, and labels used side-by-side.

questions_for_authors: How does SteerVAD compare when the 1% labeled subset is instead given to a simple weakly-supervised MIL baseline on the same backbone features? Is the win coming from the HMC or from having any supervision at all at 1%?
Does RSA select the same layer/head indices under a different frozen backbone (e.g., LLaVA-Next, Qwen-VL, VideoLLaMA)? If not, what is 'intrinsic' about these circuits?
In Table 3, was the 1% calibration subset resampled per seed, or only the training seed changed? The identical selection is only meaningful in the former case.
How does dropping the anomaly scorer's supervised BCE and using only RSA-selected raw features with a nearest-centroid rule (fully training-free) compare?

What is the variance of baselines in Table 1 under the same evaluation protocol you use, and does the +0.43% AUC / +0.87% AP over HiProbeVAD hold with matched frame sampling (F=16) and matched backbone?
How is c (the 'global context vector') defined precisely — the last hidden state of the first generated token under what prompt? Does prompt phrasing change the LAE set or the AUC materially?
calibration_check: Claims are locally supported but globally overreach: 'state-of-the-art among tuning-free' is true only if the category boundary is drawn to exclude supervised training of the HMC/scorer, and 'active geometric intervention' is a heavier framing than the elementwise scaling that is actually implemented.

significance.justification: Interesting direction (steering internal MLLM features for VAD) but the empirical delta over prior tuning-free methods is small and confined to two benchmarks.

novelty.justification: Application-level novelty for VAD, but the mechanism (identify heads, learn a context-conditioned gate, apply anisotropic scaling) is close to established activation-steering / ITI / adapter literature, which is not contrasted.

rigor.justification: Method is internally consistent and the ablations cover the main design choices, but the manifold-hypothesis framing is decorative and does not tie to any measured geometric quantity.

statistical_soundness.justification: Main comparison table has no error bars or significance tests; the +0.43% / +0.87% gains over the closest tuning-free baseline are within plausible seed noise for VAD.

calibration_honesty.justification: The 'tuning-free SOTA' framing is misleading given the HMC and scorer are trained with labeled BCE, and 'first to operationalize geometric intervention' overstates novelty relative to existing steering work.

clarity.justification: The paper is mostly readable and the pipeline is easy to follow, but the extraction shows several typos/spacing artifacts and key architectural details are deferred to appendices.

structure_compliance.justification: Standard ICLR structure (Intro, Related, Method, Experiments, Conclusion) with appropriate length; sections are well delineated.

reproducibility.justification: Backbone, optimizer, batch size, K, F, σ_g, and λ_reg are given, but critical details (context-token definition, HMC dimensions, feature position per head) sit in unseen appendices.

related_work.justification: Traditional VAD and MLLM-VAD are covered adequately, but the directly relevant activation-steering / representation-engineering / ITI / function-vector literature is missing, weakening the novelty claim.

figure_quality.justification: Captions describe a standard pipeline figure, UMAP/t-SNE manifold visualizations, and clear tables; useful but not exceptional for the claims made.

breadth_generality.justification: Only one MLLM backbone (InternVL3) and two VAD benchmarks; the paper argues LAEs are intrinsic functional circuits but does not test across backbones or datasets to support that generality.

overall_recommendation.justification: Borderline reject: promising framing and thorough ablations, but small gains without significance testing, misleading category positioning, missing related work, and single-backbone/two-dataset scope keep it below the ICLR bar as-is.
